title: Step 4 — Compliance Index
description: The index as the hub: coverage rollup, then category > subcategory rows with their actions, obligations and review state. A row opens the subcategory full screen: its actions and obligations by class, obligations filed in from elsewhere, merge and dismiss, approve and move to the next, and any requirement read against its commitment text or the ITP PDF.

What's New

1.41.0 · Oct 13, 2026

  • Lists replace Action ListsEach project now has one Lists page for action lists and commitment lists. Every list has its own page, with a searchable drawer for adding items, Select mode for removing many, and CSV export.
  • Configurable Monitoring Portal dashboardThe dashboard is now a board of widgets. Admins add them from a gallery, then resize, reorder, recolor and configure each one, and the layout is saved for the project.
  • Evidence for a whole action listChoose a component, stage the evidence, and save it to every action on that component in one step.

sections.label: Gd article
sections.html:
Scope determines how an action is distributed. A project-scoped action is performed once, centrally — for example, submitting the project-wide stormwater plan. A component-scoped action is performed independently at every applicable component — for example, installing exclusion fencing at each of 20 construction areas.

Note

Each implementation is tracked separately, with its own assignee, timeline, and evidence.

A Tenant is the organization a Beacon workspace belongs to. Beacon is multi-tenant: each tenant’s projects, documents, users, and configuration are isolated from every other tenant’s, and a user operates within a single tenant at a time.

Tenant-level settings — display labels, enabled features, notification defaults, and user roles — apply uniformly across every project the tenant owns.
